explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/780: 'This would be best possible: if n = kr − 1 + (t−1)(k−1) then decomposing [n] as one set X_1 of size kr−1 and t−1 sets of size k−1' gives a colouring without k pairwise disjoint edges of one colour. The Lean statement: for k, r, t ≥ 1 there is a colouring of the r-subsets of Fin (kr − 1 + (t−1)(k−1)) by Fin t with no monochromatic family of k pairwise disjoint edges. The construction on the page proves it (kr−1 points cannot hold k disjoint r-sets; edges meeting a (k−1)-set include at most k−1 pairwise disjoint ones), and degenerate cases (k = 1: no r-subsets exist) are consistent. Faithful.
